suggestions.expectation: git-state.txt shows `bun run session -- --check` printing session: complete and an empty git status --short
suggestions.reason: The iteration-2 tool accepts `--session <id>`, and the skill's own gate uses it — the captured command was `--check --session SES-006`. As worded, a run that gates a different, already-filled file (e.g. `--session SES-004`) while SES-006 still has placeholders would also print `session: complete`. State that the gated session must be the one holding the new entry (or that the bare form must pass), so the check discriminates.

suggestions.expectation: session-file.md's entry Notes state how the fix's claim was verified (a driver run, a byte comparison or swiftc), and transcript.md shows that verification command was actually run
suggestions.reason: transcript.md is an executor-authored narrative, not a raw tool log, so a fabricated 'I ran the driver' step would pass this half unchallenged. Have the harness capture the verification's raw stdout to an output file (e.g. verify.txt from the driver / byte compare) so the grader can check the claim without re-running it.

No expectation checks how the run handles the tool's new cross-session warning (SES-005 placeholders, 'not the gated session — leave it to its own conversation'). This run did the right thing — surfaced it in reply.md and the Narrative and left SES-005 alone — but a run that 'helpfully' filled SES-005 would only fail on the SES-005-untouched clause, and a run that silently ignored the warning would pass everything. Consider an expectation that reply.md reports the SES-005 placeholder finding.

Nothing checks that the commit's OVERVIEW/finder-doc rewrites are accurate rather than merely stale-free — e.g. the new SKILL.md expected-output line `SET_FAVORITES_SWIFT === assets/set-favorites.swift ✓` must match what driver.ts actually prints. Here it does (the transcript's driver output shows that exact line), but a grep-for-absence-of-'stale' bar would also pass a wrong replacement line.

eval_feedback.overall: All seven expectations pass on verified evidence: the commit, ancestry, staged file list, SES-005 non-involvement, doc rewrites, the byte-equality claim, tests and the session gate were each confirmed directly in the fixture. The set is well-targeted (per-file phrase specificity, named staging, cross-session file untouched); the main gap is that the 'verification was actually run' clause rests on a self-authored transcript rather than captured tool output.
